reading_the_pass: As with U1-U4: byte-identical before/after IS the pass -- the internal id each folded-id render reaches is unchanged.
MANDATORY_HONESTY_CORRECTION_C05: The audit's own worklist.json/findings.json wording for C-05 says these rows are 'byte-identical'. That is FALSE at the render level, and this unit's own new test proves it directly (not just cites the plan's numbers): SF.buildObject('contFieldSigmoid') != SF.buildObject('contFieldFore') != SF.buildObject('contFieldSurface') != SF.buildObject('contFieldQuant') != SF.buildObject('contFieldTouch') -- all 5 distinct JSON.stringify outputs, verified live. Measured ink on torus+hatch+med (from the plan, restated): contFieldSigmoid 1459.0mm(88 paths) -> contFieldFore 1808.6mm(99) -> contFieldSurface 2202.0mm(109) -> contFieldQuant 1792.2mm(98) -> contFieldTouch 3879.9mm(146, and VISUALLY CONFIRMED flooded to a near-solid disc, see visual_inspection below) -- a 51% spread between the low and high end. What IS true: they are density-inert (same relative picture across low/med/max) and dHash-close enough at plot scale to read as one family by eye -- which is exactly why the COLLAPSE (a picker-tier cut) is still the right call, but 'byte-identical' overstates a picker-level near-duplicate as render-level identity. The correct wording (already drafted in the plan itself, §1 C-05): 'near-duplicate; ink 1459-2202mm on torus/hatch/med' (the plan's own 2202 excludes contFieldTouch's 3879.9 as a separate, even-more-extreme outlier already called out with its own caveat). Fixing worklist.json/findings.json's text is U8's job per the plan's docs contract (§6) -- NOT done in this unit (out of file scope), but stated here in the loudest terms this report format allows per the coordinator's explicit instruction to verify and correct this wording.

A torus rendered as a dense continuous-field ruling pattern -- many closely-spaced concentric lines, a genuinely different mechanism-class picture from U1-U4's ladder/band/weight/bundle families. Unchanged from the pre-U5 baseline (md5-identical).

VISIBLY DENSER than contFieldSigmoid -- more rulings packed into the same silhouette, confirming the honesty correction above: this is NOT the same picture, just a similar FAMILY of picture (continuous field, same mechanism, different metric produces measurably different density).
visual_inspection.torus__hatch__contFieldTouch__med__a: LOOKED at directly. DRAMATICALLY different from the other four -- floods to a near-solid white disc with only a thin dark sliver at the centre, exactly matching the plan's own warning ('contFieldTouch floods to a solid disc at med (F-08, W-08 saturation item)') and its measured 3879.9mm ink (2.7x contFieldSigmoid's 1459.0mm). This is the strongest visual proof in this whole chain that the audit's 'byte-identical' framing for C-05 was wrong -- no one looking at this image would call it identical to the first two.

monotonicity: Not applicable as a single ordering -- fieldMetric is a 4-way enum with non-monotone ink (1459.0/1808.6/2202.0/1792.2 across screen/foreshortened/surface/quantised), and fieldFloor is a binary floor (plot/touch) with a dramatic, discontinuous jump (1459.0 -> 3879.9) that is NOT a graduated series either.
